svg.title: Terrain and boundary checks use two related grid traces
svg.desc: The upper lane shows four supercover cells and an opaque interior cell stopping terrain visibility. The lower lane shows three public sampled cells; only an orthogonal consecutive pair names a canonical boundary edge, while a diagonal pair names no edge.

g.text: Internal terrain trace: FS.GG.Game.Core.Los.supercover owns this four-connected cell list.A. internal supercover → terrain

g.title: Four supercover cells are materialized internally: source, two orthogonal intermediate cells around the corner, and target.

rect.title: Opaque intermediate terrain cell: isTransparent returns false here, so lineOfSightBy Supercover rejects the pair.

path.title: Internal walk used only for cell transparency: canonical, x-first, endpoint-exempt, and four-connected.

g.text: Reported sampled trace: SpatialQuery.lineCells uses max-axis integer interpolation and distinct cells for public reporting and boundary checks.B. reported sampled line → boundaries
max-axis interpolation; diagonal pairs name no edge

g.title: Three sampled cells are reported for these endpoints. This list is smaller than the four-cell supercover.

path.title: Sampled path: its first pair is orthogonal and can resolve to an Edge; its second pair is diagonal and cannot.

line.title: Canonical sampled edge: Edges.edgeBetween returns Some for this orthogonally adjacent pair, so boundary permeability is consulted.

path.title: Diagonal sampled pair: Edges.edgeBetween returns None, and Option.forall therefore treats this segment as boundary-passable.

svg.text: Both predicates must pass. The model keeps the traces separate so its explanation matches SpatialQuery.
